s: an off-the-radar coffeehouse where the trends of a century seem to have stopped at the door
w: A Mariahilf coffeehouse a few streets from the tourist cafés, full of Viennese regulars and seemingly unbothered by the passage of time or trend. No spectacle here, just a properly kept Viennese Kaffeehaus doing what it has always done.
_facts: Located at Otto-Bauer-Gasse 5, 1060 Wien, Mariahilf
Traditional Viennese coffeehouse known for its local, off-tourist-track regulars

s: a café hidden among the trees of the Kronprinzengarten, behind the crowds at Schönbrunn
w: Set among the trees of the Kronprinzengarten inside Schönbrunn Palace Park, this seasonal café (open April to October) sits far enough from the palace's main paths to feel like a genuine escape from the crowds, coffee and cake served with the quiet of the surrounding gardens rather than a view of a queue.
_facts: Located in the Kronprinzengarten, Schönbrunn Palace Park, 1130 Wien
Open seasonally, April to October
Set apart from Schönbrunn's main visitor paths within the palace gardens

s: a bookshop, café and bar with 4,000 books and no laptops allowed
w: A café, bookshop and bar rolled into one on Gumpendorfer Straße since 2004, its shelves holding some 4,000 books for sale or browsing around mismatched secondhand furniture. Laptops are pointedly not welcome -- a deliberate stand for conversation and reading over remote work in one of Vienna's more determinedly analogue rooms.
_facts: Located at Gumpendorfer Straße 10-12, 1060 Wien, Mariahilf
Combines a bookshop (around 4,000 titles), café and bar
Open since 2004
Laptop-free policy

s: a 1950s-styled coffeehouse behind an unremarkable Postgasse facade
w: An unremarkable street-level facade on Postgasse conceals a room styled around 1950s design, long known as a gathering point for Vienna's artists and writers. Traditional coffeehouse service persists alongside a more nonconformist, creative undertone than the grander imperial-era cafés.
_facts: Located at Postgasse 2, 1010 Wien, Innere Stadt
Interior styled around 1950s design
Long associated with Vienna's artistic and literary community

s: a cult, vinyl-soundtracked refuge with decades of patina on Ungargasse
w: A small, cult-followed café on Ungargasse in Landstraße, its walls and furniture carrying a patina that comes only from decades of the same regulars. Vinyl on the stereo and a student-intellectual, slightly hideaway atmosphere set it apart from the polish of the central coffeehouses.
_facts: Located at Ungargasse 10, 1030 Wien, Landstraße
Known for playing vinyl records and a worn, long-accumulated interior character
Has a cult local following

s: a shabby, gothic-tinged bar on a curiously quiet Spittelberg square
w: A deliberately grungy, alternative bar on Sankt-Ulrichs-Platz, an oddly underpopulated square in the otherwise busy Spittelberg quarter. A red star glows over a fetchingly shabby, gothic-edged interior; the terrace outside carries an outsized sense of place for such a small square.
_facts: Located at Sankt-Ulrichs-Platz 5, 1070 Wien, Neubau/Spittelberg
Known for a deliberately worn, alternative gothic-styled interior
Has an outdoor terrace on the square

s: a takeaway coffee window pouring lattes into chocolate-dipped waffle cones
w: A literal window onto Griechengasse -- no seating, just a hatch -- serving the "Fensterccino": a milky latte poured straight into a waffle cone dipped in chocolate, which melts as you drink. Open since 2011 and filling something like 130,000 orders a year, it's become one of Vienna's most photographed and most expensive cups of coffee.
_facts: Located at Griechengasse 10, 1010 Wien, Innere Stadt
Takeaway-only coffee window, open since 2011
Signature drink is the "Fensterccino": latte served in a chocolate-dipped waffle cone
Reportedly fills over 130,000 orders per year

s: a café hidden on the roof of Vienna's imperial Palace of Justice
w: A café tucked onto the rooftop of the Justizpalast -- Vienna's grand Palace of Justice -- open weekday mornings to whoever knows to look for it, well above the tourist sightlines of the Ringstrasse. Imperial architecture underfoot, strudel on the table, and a view most visitors never learn exists.
_facts: Located at Schmerlingplatz 11, 1010 Wien, on the roof of the Justizpalast (Palace of Justice)
Open Monday to Friday, 7:30am-4pm
Known for its rooftop setting above the Ringstrasse
